newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks set for bumpy ride this week.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks set for bumpy ride this week.

text.p: Further turbulence is in store for the battered Thai bourse this week as more foreign investors are expected to exit on worries about the economy and the quality of the new government after polls, analysts said.

In four straight falls last week, hefty gains of nearly 5.0 percent posted last Monday were wiped out. The market closed down 21.65 points at 1004.89 points on Friday, the lowest level since September 11.
Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa's decision to dissolve parliament and call fresh elections on November 17 spurred Monday's rise, the highest made in a single day in 19 months.
Analysts said that sharp rise may have been overdone, and there was now little positive news in store to revive the flagging bourse.

"I'm hearing that foreign investors are coming out of the banks, which account for about 49 percent of the entire profits made by companies in the market and 23 percent of the SET index," said Kanjanee Kangwanpornsiri, assistant managing director at Thai Fuji Finance and Securities. "We are advising short-term investors to stay on the sidelines at the moment, and that medium-term investors reduce their portfolios."
The economic worries follow a sharp slowdown in the national economy this year after a decade of robust growth, with exports falling and the current account deficit widening, analysts said.

The market was also squeamish about the prospects of rising inflation because floods over the past week were likely to push up food prices and spending was sure to rise ahead of the November election, they added.
Investors were also concerned about the quality of any new government and its capability to tide over economic woes after the polls, the analysts said.

"Foreigners are likely to continue to sell in the week ahead because of their concern about the Thai economy and the stability of a new government to be formed after the November 17 elections. They've lost confidence," said analyst Virat Tippanontakul of First Asia Securities.
However, some analysts said the bourse could react positively to Wall Street's rally on Friday, but gains would probably be limited.
"Wall Street's surge on Friday will certainly add positive news to the market but local economic and political concerns will hinder agressive buying," said a broker at Nava Finance and Securities.
News that Thailand's top bank, Bangkok Bank Plc, would raise deposit rates by 25 basis points soon and that other banks might follow could dampen sentiment, analysts said.
"I don't see a lot of good news bringing people in," said David Sandison, head of foreign sales at Jardine Fleming Thanakom Securities. "We are pretty bearish on this market at the moment."
Brokers said they hoped that price-earnings ratios in the market were now low enough to attract long-term investors.

"We haven't really seen any differentiation, there has been very solid selling from all quarters," said a senior analyst at Krungthai Thanakit Plc, "But I think the potential for much more downside is limited now."
